Think about what happens when you hold something physically heavy in your hands. It demands your attention. You can't ignore it. You feel its presence. You have to deal with it carefully.

The adjective weighty takes that same feeling — the feeling of heaviness — and applies it to things that are not always physical. Something weighty is something that carries real, serious significance or importance, something you cannot brush aside lightly.

Weighty has a few related uses, and they all revolve around the idea of "heaviness" — either literal or metaphorical.

1. Physically Heavy (Literal Use)

In its most straightforward sense, weighty simply means heavy in physical weight.

"The workers struggled to lift the weighty stone blocks."

This use is not very common in everyday speech. Most people just say "heavy." But "weighty" still works here, and you will encounter it occasionally in writing.

2. Serious, Important, and Significant (Most Common Use)

This is by far the most frequent meaning. When something is called weighty, it means it is serious, significant, and deserving of careful thought and attention. It is the kind of thing you cannot handle carelessly or dismiss without consideration.

"The scientists gathered to discuss a weighty question: Is there life on other planets?"

"The president had to make a weighty decision that would affect millions of people."

"They spent hours debating weighty matters of law and justice."

Notice the pattern: weighty things are not trivial. They are not small talk or minor inconveniences. They carry real consequence — in life, in relationships, in society, in history. When you describe something as weighty, you are signalling to your listener: pay attention, this matters.

3. Difficult to Bear — A Burden

When you carry something heavy for a long time, it becomes exhausting. It weighs you down. In the same way, weighty can describe something that is burdensome — difficult to carry emotionally, morally, or mentally.

"She accepted the weighty responsibility of caring for her entire family."

"The guilt was weighty, pressing down on him with every passing day."

Here, "weighty" conveys not just importance, but also the strain and heaviness that comes with it. The thing is not just significant — it costs something.

4. Powerful and Convincing (For Arguments, Reasons, Evidence)

When used to describe an argument, reason, or piece of evidence, weighty means difficult to ignore or dismiss — convincing and forceful.

"She made a weighty argument that the policy needed to change."

"The defence lawyer presented weighty evidence in favour of his client."

A weighty argument is one that lands with force and carries real logical or moral power behind it. It is not easily brushed aside.

5. Influential and Authoritative (For People or Opinions)

Weighty can also describe a person, opinion, or voice that holds great authority, influence, or importance in a particular area.

"A weighty figure in the world of science, she had published over 200 papers."

"His weighty opinion swayed the entire committee."

When a person is "weighty," they are not just important in a vague sense — they carry clout. Their words and decisions have real impact.

Every meaning of weighty traces back to the same idea: something that has real substance and cannot be taken lightly.

UseWhat it means

Here is the thread in words: a heavy object demands your physical effort. A heavy topic demands your mental and emotional effort. A heavy responsibility demands your time and sacrifice. A heavy argument demands your serious consideration. A heavy person demands your respect and attention. That thread — you cannot take this lightly — runs through every use of weighty.

Weighty is a slightly formal word. You are more likely to read it in books, newspapers, and essays than to hear it in casual conversation. In everyday speech, people tend to say "serious," "important," or "big" instead. But in writing, weighty adds a layer of gravitas — a sense that something is not just important, but deeply important.

It also carries a neutral-to-slightly-solemn tone. You wouldn't use "weighty" to describe something exciting or joyful. Weighty things are serious things.
What Weighty Is Often Used With

To get a feel for the word, here are the kinds of nouns you will typically see it paired with:

  • Weighty matter / issue / subject / topic — something serious that requires careful thought
  • Weighty decision / choice — a decision with major consequences
  • Weighty responsibility / burden / obligation — something difficult and important to carry
  • Weighty argument / evidence / reason — something convincing and forceful
  • Weighty question / debate — a serious, significant discussion
  • Weighty figure / authority / voice — a person or entity of great influence

Weighty = heavy in importance, seriousness, or significance. It describes things that cannot be taken lightly — whether that is a physical object, a decision, a responsibility, an argument, or a person's influence. The word carries a formal, serious tone and is more common in writing than in casual speech. It always says: this has real substance; handle with care.
